headline: 5 die, 839 hospitalised as dengue cases cross last year’s total by August
summary: Bangladesh is facing a severe dengue outbreak as the number of infections has already surpassed the total cases recorded in the previous year by August.
details: Five more people have died from dengue fever in the last 24 hours, while 839 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.
The current surge in infections is alarming, with the total number of dengue cases in 2024 already exceeding the total number of cases recorded throughout the entire previous year by August.
Health authorities are monitoring the situation closely as hospitals continue to see a high volume of patients requiring urgent care.
The rapid increase in cases highlights the ongoing struggle to control the mosquito-borne illness during the rainy season.

headline_marked: 6 million [[CVs of Bangladeshis for sale]] on Dark Web
headline: 6 million CVs of Bangladeshis for sale on Dark Web
summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen data from BDJobs, though the platform denies any breach of its own systems.
details: A hacker group calling themselves 'Madarx' has advertised the sale of 6 million CVs of Bangladeshi citizens on the website 'DarkForums.ru'.
The hackers claim the data was sourced from the BDJobs database, including names, phone numbers, addresses, emails, educational qualifications, and work experience.
The group is offering a copy of the database for $1,000, limiting the sale to a maximum of five buyers, with payments accepted via Paytm, Wise, PayU, and Binance.
To support their claim, the group released 148 sample CVs. Analysis shows most of these are old, with many last updated between 2011 and 2017.
BDJobs founder and CEO Fahim Mashrur has denied the data leak from their website, stating that the platform prioritizes user security and has controls over who can view profiles.
Mashrur noted that while hundreds of thousands of registered recruiters can view candidate data for hiring, any recruiter who sells this data to a third party would face legal action.
Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha warned that such data allows criminals to create full digital profiles for targeted phishing, fake job offers, identity theft, and financial fraud.
caption:
6 million CVs of Bangladeshis are being sold on the Dark Web for $1,000. Is your personal data safe?

A hacker group calling themselves 'Madarx' has advertised the sale of 6 million CVs of Bangladeshi citizens on the website 'DarkForums.ru'.

The hackers claim the data was sourced from the BDJobs database, including names, phone numbers, addresses, emails, educational qualifications, and work experience.

The group is offering a copy of the database for $1,000, limiting the sale to a maximum of five buyers, with payments accepted via Paytm, Wise, PayU, and Binance.

To support their claim, the group released 148 sample CVs. Analysis shows most of these are old, with many last updated between 2011 and 2017.

BDJobs founder and CEO Fahim Mashrur has denied the data leak from their website, stating that the platform prioritizes user security and has controls over who can view profiles.

Mashrur noted that while hundreds of thousands of registered recruiters can view candidate data for hiring, any recruiter who sells this data to a third party would face legal action.

Cyber security expert Tanveer Hassan Zoha warned that such data allows criminals to create full digital profiles for targeted phishing, fake job offers, identity theft, and financial fraud.
